title: Heatmaps Show Where We're Looking
content: Eyetracking heatmaps appear as red and yellow blobs where viewers spend the most time looking.Norman Rockwell'sFreedom from Want,courtesyDan HillAccording to Dan Hill, "If there's a face involved, as much as seventy percent or more of all the gaze activity goes to the face(s) present."Hill notes that in the paintingAmerican Gothicby Grant Wood, even the pitchfork and the man's hand don't compete with the faces.We use faces to form our impression of people, Hill says. "We're always looking for clues about their social status, their mood and overall personality."Images from the book "First Blush: People's Intuitive Reactions to Famous Art" by Dan Hill
